children: climbed 20% in early Thursday after its latest quarterly figures topped Wall Street estimates and the company raised its outlook for the year.
Adjusted earnings came in at 62 cents a share, ahead of the 45-cent analyst consensus. Revenue reached $1.55 billion, up 35% from a year earlier and above the $1.48 billion estimate.

Snowflake also pointed to increasing adoption of CoCo, its artificial intelligence coding agent. The product had 9,100 customer accounts by the end of the quarter, adding more than 2,000 during the period.

For the fiscal third quarter, management expects product revenue of $1.59 billion, compared with the $1.50 billion Street forecast. Its full-year product revenue projection rose to $6.07 billion from $5.84 billion, while the adjusted operating margin target increased to 14.5% from 13.5%.
The stronger forecast and AI-product traction could support Snowflake's valuation if growth remains on track.

title: Why Is Snowflake Stock Soaring Today
